subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Accessibility Test Reporting
description: A short lesson to help you apply Accessibility Test Reporting.

hook.text: An audit finds 200 issues. The team is overwhelmed and does nothing. The report lacked severity and priority.

buildup.text: Effective reports categorize issues by severity, WCAG criterion, user impact, and remediation effort.

discovery.text: Prioritizing by user impact ensures the most harmful barriers are fixed first, not just the easiest.

twist.text: Screenshots and screen reader recordings help developers understand barriers without assistive tech experience.

climax.text: A prioritized report with clear reproduction steps leads to 80% of critical issues fixed in two sprints.

punchline.text: A good report drives action. A bad report drives paralysis.

quiz.question: How should accessibility issues be prioritized?
options: By user impact and barrier severity
